ASTRAVITAL: Mission Medical Intelligence

ASTRAVITAL is an interactive prototype of a health-monitoring platform for astronauts on long-duration missions. Set in a simulated Mars expedition (MARS-01), it brings crew health information into one connected workspace so a flight surgeon or astronaut can understand it at a glance.

Problem: On deep-space missions, crews are far from Earth, communication is delayed and medical help is limited. Health signals are often tracked separately, making gradual changes hard to spot early.

Solution: The core is an interactive Astronaut Digital Twin, a living anatomical model. Users can explore 11 body systems through layers such as skeleton, muscular, cardiovascular, nervous system and a health-risk heatmap. Selecting a region opens indicators, trends, spaceflight risks, examination history, observations and guidance. Readings are compared with the astronaut's personal baseline; in the demo, a resting heart rate of 65.6 bpm against a 58.1 bpm baseline is flagged as a mild drift. A 13-module workspace also covers AI health intelligence, cognitive performance, mental wellbeing, environmental monitoring and preventive healthcare.

Responsible design: All data is simulated. The prototype makes no diagnoses, is not a medical device, is not endorsed by NASA and does not replace flight surgeons.

Built with AI: Created entirely with AI apps and websites and published on Framer.

Live prototype: https://astravital.framer.website/
details:
ASTRAVITAL: Mission Medical Intelligence

ASTRAVITAL is an interactive prototype of a health-monitoring platform for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It is set in a simulated Mars expedition (MARS-01), currently in the transit phase on Mission Day 147. It shows how a flight surgeon or crew member could view, track and understand astronaut health in one connected workspace. All data is simulated, and the site says clearly that it is not a medical device, is not endorsed by NASA and does not replace flight surgeons.

Mission workspace and navigation

The interface is a dashboard-style workspace. A top bar shows the active mission, the mission day and phase, an online status indicator and an Emergency Access button. A sidebar lists 13 modules:

  • Mission Command Center
  • Astronaut Digital Twin
  • Medical Body Scanner
  • Health Monitoring
  • AI Health Intelligence
  • Cognitive Performance
  • Mental Wellbeing
  • Environmental Monitoring
  • Mission Health Timeline
  • Preventive Healthcare
  • Medical Operations
  • Crew Health Network
  • Medical Knowledge Center
  • Settings

A status line reads “All systems operational”, and the footer tags the build as Local Prototype v1.0.

Astronaut Digital Twin (the core feature)

The main screen is a living digital twin of the astronaut Alex Morgan (AST-001). It shows an interactive anatomical map with a mission-elapsed-time clock. Users can:

  • Switch between layers: Anatomical, Skeleton, Muscular, Cardiovascular, Nervous system, Health-risk heatmap and Examination.
  • Rotate between front and back views, or reset the view.
  • Select any of 11 connected regions: brain, eyes, heart, lungs, blood vessels, musculoskeletal system, bones, kidneys, digestive system, skin and immune system.
  • Read the colour-coded legend, where each region is marked either routine or attention.
  • Start a Guided Demo that walks a first-time viewer through the twin.

Region intelligence panel

Selecting a region opens a detail panel with six tabs: Indicators, Trends, Spaceflight Risks, Examination History, Observations and Guidance. The Cardiovascular example shows a resting heart rate of 65.6 bpm, which is 7.5 bpm above the astronaut’s personal baseline of 58.1 bpm. A trend line runs from Day 118 to Day 147 and flags a mild resting heart-rate drift over the last 8 days. The wording is careful: it suggests reading the drift alongside sleep and recovery trends and states that no diagnosis is inferred. An “Open in Scanner” button links the region to the Medical Body Scanner.

Summary tiles

Four tiles give the astronaut’s status at a glance:

  • Systems monitored: 11
  • Overall status: Stable, with 2 observations for attention
  • Last examination: Day 140, a routine mission assessment
  • Next health review: Day 150, a cardiovascular follow-up with the flight surgeon

Design and tone

The look is a dark, mission-control style. The language is informational and cautious, with “Simulated data” and “Informational only. Not a diagnosis.” repeated on the key screens.

Built entirely with AI

ASTRAVITAL was created entirely with AI apps and websites. The concept, content, layout and design were produced using [list your tools here, e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Framer AI], and the site is published on Framer. No traditional manual coding was needed. It shows how a complex, data-rich product concept can go from idea to a working interactive prototype using AI tools alone.
